chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A group of captives from Yemen was brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When they reached Al-Juhfa, their expenses ran out, so they sold a female slave from the captives whose mother was with them. When they arrived before the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he heard her crying and said, "What is this?" They said, "O Messenger of Allah, we needed expenses, so we sold her daughter." He sent for her price, and she was brought to him. He said, "Sell them both together or keep them both together."'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet do when captives sold a mother and daughter separately due to lack of funds?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s sensitivity to emotional distress as a legal indicator, where the sound of the daughter’s crying prompted him to rectify the separation of the mother-daughter pair. This incident establishes a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of family members within the captive population, emphasizing that financial necessity does not override the preservation of kinship ties (silat al-rahim).
